name: MIC29302AWD-TR
title: MIC29302A: 3A low-dropout adjustable regulator, 1.24V to 15V output, TO-263-5 and TO-252-5
summary: A positive linear regulator with a PNP pass transistor that delivers up to 3A with 560 mV typical dropout at full load. It runs from 3V to 16V and its output is set from 1.24V to 15V by two resistors on the ADJ pin, which regulates to 1.24V; output accuracy is ±2% over line, load and temperature. A logic-level EN pin shuts it down to 32 µA. It limits current, shuts down when hot, and withstands reversed input and reversed insertion. It comes in 5-lead TO-263 (D2Pak) and TO-252 (D-Pak) packages for -40°C to +125°C junction temperature.
key_figures: 5 mA typ at 750 mA, 60 mA typ at 3A

notes: The name reads MIC29302A, then an output-voltage field left blank for the adjustable part, W for the -40°C to +125°C range (RoHS compliant with the high-melting-solder exemption), D for TO-252 or U for TO-263, and -TR for tape and reel.
The -TR suffix is an ordering code only and does not appear in the marking.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: A 3.3V supply brought down to 2.5V. EN is wired to IN so the regulator runs whenever input is present; R1 and R2 divide the output onto ADJ, and with 191Ω over 187Ω the output sits near 2.5V. CIN sits across the input, and the polarised CL across the output keeps the loop stable.

circuits.title: Adjustable regulator with resistors (Figure 4-2)
circuits.description: The general adjustable connection: EN and IN share the supply, OUT feeds the load and the top of the R1-R2 divider, and the divider tap goes to ADJ. R1 follows from R2 and the wanted output by Equation 4-1. A 10μF polarised capacitor decouples the input and a 22μF polarised capacitor the output.

circuits.title: Load transient response test circuit (Figure 2-27)
circuits.description: The connection used for the load transient measurements: 3.3V in, 2.5V out set by 191Ω over 187Ω, EN tied to IN, CIN on the input and the polarised CL on the output.

equations.note: Example: 3.0A, VIN = 3.3V, VOUT = 2.5V gives PD = 3.0A × (1.05 × 3.3V − 2.5V) = 2.9W; in TO-252 at TA = +75°C, TJ = 35°C/W × 2.9W + 75°C = 176.5°C, beyond the +125°C limit.

operation.text: The output device is a PNP transistor made in the Super βeta PNP process, so the dropout is set by its collector-emitter saturation and not by a base-emitter drop. Its base drive scales with load and is about 1% of the load current. Full-load dropout is 560 mV typical.

Current limiting is linear: in overload the output current is held constant. Thermal shutdown turns the regulator off when the die passes +125°C. A voltage above the set output may be forced onto OUT without current flowing back into the part. It also survives reversed input polarity and leads inserted the wrong way round.

EN is a logic input with TTL/CMOS thresholds (0.8V low, 2.4V high); tied to VIN the regulator stays on. Turning on takes roughly 20 µA flowing into EN. EN must not float. Disabled, the part draws 32 µA with 16V on the input.

An output capacitor is required for stability and low noise; the value needed grows with load current, and 10 µF is stable at full load. Low ESR is not needed and aluminium electrolytics work; capacitors of very low ESR can make the loop unstable. Tantalum is the choice where a fast response to load steps matters.
When the supply feeding IN has a high AC impedance, fit 0.1 µF from IN to GND.
Set for a 3.3V output, the regulator keeps its full transient response down to a 4.2V input and still regulates partly down to 3.8V.

At least 10 mA of load is needed for regulation and to swamp leakage across temperature; with less, the output creeps up. The divider R1 + R2 can be sized so it alone draws this 10 mA, which suits loads that vary widely.
Two resistors set the output anywhere from 1.24V to 15V, by Equation 4-1.

Thermal design starts from the highest ambient temperature, the output current, the output voltage and the input voltage: work out PD, then the heatsink by Equation 4-3. Where the lowest input voltage is well above the dropout, a resistor in series with the input can take part of the heat; then put at least 0.1 µF right between the input and the regulator ground. The θJA of TO-252 holds for a board with 2 oz/ft² (70 µm) copper and 100 mm² of copper area for the part.

Load-step response is given for a 200 mA to 3A step with 1000 µF on the output; line-step response for a 5V to 15V input step at 3A load with 10 µF and with 1000 µF on the output. Figure 2-27 is the load transient test circuit.
